summary.en: Distinguish tokens, lexemes, and patterns, preserve tokens across buffers, and locate lexical errors.
summary.bn: টোকেন, লেক্সিম ও প্যাটার্ন আলাদা করো, বাফার বদলালেও শব্দ ঠিক রাখো এবং ভুলের অবস্থান বের করো।

notes: Implementations were run with Python 3.12.14 and use only the standard library.

examples.title: Whole-word token categories
examples.explanationHtml: let is a keyword, but printable is an identifier. The whole word 2roll matches neither the identifier nor integer rule.

examples.title: An identifier crossing chunks
examples.explanationHtml: mar remains pending when the first chunk ends. The next chunk completes marks before =. The final roll is emitted when all chunks are exhausted.

examples.title: A line-numbered character error
examples.explanationHtml: The first newline resets the column. In roll=@7;, @ is the sixth character on line 2, so the diagnostic identifies 2:6.

practice.title: Classify complete words
practice.statementHtml: Read one word per line, including possibly empty lines. Print KEYWORD, IDENTIFIER, INTEGER, or ERROR for each. Use the rules above; this is whole-word classification.
hints: Check reserved words before identifier syntax.

practice.title: Locate every at-sign
practice.statementHtml: Read arbitrary text until end of input. Print line:column for each @ using one-based character columns; newline resets the column. Print nothing when none occurs.
hints: Update position for every character, including spaces.

practice.title: A block boundary
practice.statementHtml: A buffer ends with stu and the next starts dent;. Show the two emitted tokens.
hints: Join pending letters before processing punctuation.
practice.answerHtml: The joined spelling is student, so emit ID(student). The semicolon ends that name and becomes SEMI. The refill between stu and dent is not part of the language syntax.

practice.title: Recovery choice
practice.statementHtml: A scanner encounters @ at position 3:8 and is asked to continue. Describe a safe next action.
hints: A continuing scanner must not remain on the same character.
practice.answerHtml: Report an unsupported @ at 3:8, consume that character, and advance the column to 9. Resume recognition at the next position. Keep already recognised tokens, but do not pretend @ was a valid operator.

quiz.prompt: In ID(marks), which part is the lexeme?
quiz.explanation: The lexeme is the concrete spelling; ID names its category.

quiz.prompt: What does an identifier pattern describe?
quiz.explanation: A spelling rule can be checked without knowing runtime values.
options: The final value of every variable

quiz.prompt: Why should printable not begin with a PRINT token?
quiz.explanation: The scanner reads the full identifier before keyword lookup.
options: Its full spelling is a longer identifier

quiz.prompt: What should happen when a buffer ends halfway through marks?
quiz.explanation: A block boundary is a storage event, not a token delimiter.

quiz.prompt: Which token attribute is most useful for an unknown-name diagnostic?
quiz.explanation: Later analysis needs to know which name was used and where.

quiz.prompt: What guarantees progress after reporting an illegal character?
quiz.explanation: Recovery needs a forward step; stopping is another defined policy.

quiz.prompt: Does recognising all tokens prove valid statement structure?
quiz.explanation: The parser still needs to check how tokens are arranged.
options: Only if there are no numbers

quiz.prompt: After this newline, which line and column are printed?
quiz.code:
line, column = 1, 4
line, column = line + 1, 1
print(f"{line}:{column}")
quiz.explanation: A newline increments the line and resets the one-based column.

quiz.prompt: How many token categories are represented in this list?
quiz.code:
tokens = [("ID", "x"), ("PLUS", "+"), ("ID", "y")]
print(len({kind for kind, text in tokens}))
quiz.explanation: Two spellings share ID, while PLUS is a different category.

quiz.prompt: Which identifier survives joining these two buffer fragments?
quiz.explanation: The trailing = is punctuation and does not belong to the identifier.

keyPoints.en: A lexeme is the spelling found in source text.
A token carries a category and useful attributes.
keyPoints.bn: টোকেনে ধরন আর দরকারি তথ্য থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Patterns describe the allowed token spellings.
keyPoints.bn: প্যাটার্ন বলে কোন বানান টোকেন হিসেবে চলবে।

keyPoints.en: An input-block boundary does not end a token.
keyPoints.bn: ইনপুটের ব্লক শেষ হলেই টোকেন শেষ হয় না।

keyPoints.en: Skipping whitespace must still update source positions.
keyPoints.bn: ফাঁকা জায়গা বাদ দিলেও লাইন ও কলামের হিসাব বদলাতে হয়।

examQuestions.question: Define token, lexeme, and pattern using let marks=85;.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
Tokens for let marks=85; with one-based positions
LexemeToken categoryAttributePosition
letLETReserved word1:1
marksIDName marks1:5
=ASSIGNAssignment operator1:10
85INTInteger value 851:11
;SEMIStatement terminator1:13

A pattern is the spelling rule, such as one or more ASCII digits for INT.

examQuestions.question: Explain a two-buffer scanner and how it handles a token crossing the boundary.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Alternate two input regions while tracking token-start and forward positions. Refilling must preserve any characters needed by an unfinished token. Distinguish a region sentinel from true end of file, and allow a spill or growth strategy for tokens longer than the available regions.

examQuestions.question: Explain lexical error reporting and recovery for an unsupported character.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Record the bad character and its line and column. A continuing policy can emit a diagnostic, consume one character, update its position, and resume. It must not stall. A stop-on-first-error policy is also valid when stated explicitly.
